messages:
amy_support: ACME just opened an escalation — streaming p99 TTFB spiked after last night's deploy, non-stream total latency looks fine. Customer reports first chunk often delayed ~1.2s and p99 ~3.4s.
leo_eng: thanks. do we have an example request + model + headers? is customer using SSE or h2? any repro curl?
amy_support: SSE from their mobile SDK. sample request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/streams
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Model: redwood-open-v1
Body: {"prompt":"...","stream":true}
```
leo_eng: copying. can you also paste a raw trace id from their session? we'll pull worker traces.
amy_support: trace: trace_0a9f45 (from their support log). they attached client-side timings: connect 80ms, tls 60ms, server-first-byte 1250ms. non-stream total = 1.35s typically, so bulk work time not huge, but first chunk is delayed.
maria_sre: looking at infra traces for trace_0a9f45 — I see the request fanouts to 8 inference shards (fanout_count=8), and all shards report waiting on kv-cache-warmup locks for ~900-1200ms before any chunk was emitted.
leo_eng: that matches. streaming first chunk waits for at least one shard to produce prefix flush before the router emits? we have heuristics to avoid interleaving partial prefixes but might be too strict for high-fanout paths.
amy_support: customer says this started after deploy 4125679999 (yesterday 22:30 UTC).
pm_jordan: @leo_eng @maria_sre priority high — customer on paid enterprise tier. want proposed mitigations quick.
maria_sre: immediate mitigations: 1) enable per-route 'emit-first-chunk-on-any' flag to allow first chunk as soon as first shard has output (this trades interleaving risk for lower TTFB). 2) reduce streaming batch wait (flush_window_ms) from 8ms -> 0ms for this model/tenant. 3) temporary rollback of deploy 4125679999 if config change not safe.
leo_eng: for root cause I'm seeing a change in the kernel scheduler that added a short barrier when a model has >4 partitions to synchronize KV cache warmup; intended to reduce tail duplication but it increases TTFB for streaming cases. change was gated but feature flag accidentally flipped for prod.
amy_support: can you confirm which commits/function toggles? customer wants ETA on fix.
leo_eng: culprit: commit abc1f2d7 — flag name run.sync_kv_warmup=true. Revert patch or gate by request.streaming=true. I'll submit a hotfix to gate the behavior behind partitioned-fanout AND streaming=false.
maria_sre: rolling mitigation plan:
- short term (within 30m): set per-tenant config to flush_window_ms=0 and enable emit-first-chunk-on-any for the tenant via console. will give immediate TTFB relief.
- medium (1-4h): push hotfix to gate sync_kv_warmup behind streaming flag, canary to 5% traffic.
- long (days): add fanout-aware streaming heuristic that picks between strict-merge vs optimistic-first-chunk based on observed interleaving rate.
leo_eng: commands I ran to inspect traces:
```
redwood traces get trace_0a9f45 --format json | jq '.spans[] | select(.name=="kv_warmup")'
# shows 8 spans with duration ~1s
```
amy_support: customer tried toggling non-streaming and they see first byte immediate but then total time increases slightly. they prefer lower TTFB (user experience for chat).
pm_jordan: go ahead with the short-term per-tenant config change, notify customer and monitor p95/p99 for 30m.
maria_sre: applied tenant config change at 4125680005 -> flush_window_ms=0 and emit-first-chunk-on-any=true for tenant acme-tenant-id.
amy_support: updated customer at 22:40 UTC — they reported initial improvement, many sessions now show first chunk ~120-160ms.
leo_eng: I'll prepare the hotfix PR now: revert gating to only sync when streaming=false for partitioned models. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/3245 (WIP).
maria_sre: starting canary rollout for PR build at 4125680500 to 5% traffic. oncall_bot: deploy 4125680600 started -> success in canary. :thumbsup:
oncall_bot: NOTE: deploy 4125680600 succeeded for canary targets.
leo_eng: monitoring note — after mitigation p99 TTFB dropped from 3.4s -> 180ms for sampled sessions. we'll keep eyes on interleaving errors and token ordering regressions.
amy_support: customer happy with short-term fix, asked for timeline for permanent fix. I told them medium-term ~3 hours for canary then gradual rollout and long-term in next sprint.
pm_jordan: owners: leo_eng (root cause + PR), maria_sre (rollout + metrics), amy_support (customer comms). next update in 45m or when canary finished. :eyes:
